title: After Trump’s Rout, Will Global Trade Keep Defying Politics?
gist: Gavekal argues global goods trade volume is growing at its fastest pace in 15 years (ex-post-Covid) despite Trump's war and tariffs, driven by AI-equipment demand and trade diversion, with the WTO seeing faster growth in 2027. Key risks are an AI bust and a backlash against Chinese exports that could hit US$4.5trn in 2026, though the world remains addicted to Chinese goods.

themes.theme: Trade resilience despite tariffs and war

insights.claim: Despite war and Trump-era tariffs that have politically damaged President Donald Trump and the Republican Party, global trade continues to defy these geopolitical headwinds.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tariff/war headlines have not translated into a trade contraction; avoid shorting trade-sensitive assets on political noise alone.
insights.quote: global trade continues to defy these geopolitical headwinds
insights.locator: War and tariffs have knocked President

insights.claim: Global goods trade volume (not just value inflated by higher oil and microchip prices) is growing at its fastest pace in 15 years, excluding the post-Covid rebound.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Trade strength is real-volume, not merely a price effect, supporting shipping, ports and export-heavy economies.
insights.quote: goods trade volume is growing at its fastest pace in 15 years, excluding the post-Covid rebound
insights.locator: War and tariffs have knocked President

insights.claim: The expansion in global trade is driven by strong worldwide demand for artificial-intelligence equipment and by exporters finding alternative markets and adapting to supply-chain disruptions.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Trade growth is concentrated in AI hardware plus trade diversion, so beneficiaries are AI supply-chain exporters and rerouting hubs.
insights.quote: driven both by strong global appetite for artificial-intelligence equipment and by exporters finding alternative markets
insights.locator: War and tariffs have knocked President

insights.claim: The World Trade Organization forecasts that global trade growth will accelerate further in 2027.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Official consensus points to a stronger 2027 trade year, raising the bar for a downside surprise.
insights.quote: The World Trade Organization forecasts that trade growth will accelerate further in 2027.

themes.theme: AI capex as swing factor for trade

insights.claim: If the AI investment boom turns to bust, global trade growth will slow sharply in both volume and value terms; conversely a sustained AI boom would keep supplying demand.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Global trade momentum is effectively a leveraged bet on AI capex; monitor hyperscaler spending as a leading indicator for trade volumes.
insights.quote: if the AI boom turns to bust, trade growth will slow sharply in both volume and value terms

themes.theme: China export surge and backlash risk

insights.claim: Chinese exports could reach a scarcely believable US$4.5 trillion in 2026, and a political backlash against them would compound any trade slowdown.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: China's export scale is a growing political target; protectionist backlash is a key tail risk layered on AI-cycle risk.
insights.quote: A political backlash against Chinese exports, which could reach a scarcely believable US$4.5trn in 2026, would compound the slowdown.

insights.claim: The world will struggle to break its addiction to Chinese goods, limiting how far political backlash can actually reduce Chinese export volumes.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Bet on durability of Chinese export share over decoupling narratives.
insights.quote: the world will struggle to break its addiction to Chinese goods
